The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident took place on 22.12.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 22.12.2023 at about 08.30 a.m., petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EU-7084 which was droven by her husband slowly and cautiously with observing all traffic rules and regulations, when approached Om Road took 'U' turn near Battarahalli Junction, at that time the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265 came in high speed, rash and negligent manner came against the one way in the opposite direction without observing the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Bowring Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as house maid and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her future income.
Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent has appeared before the court.

Hence, placed Exparte.
4.

On the basis of above pleadings, the points that arise for my consideration:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265 on 22.12.2023 at about 08.30 a.m., near Battarahalli Signal Om Road towards Hosakote K. R. Puram, Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?

sentences.text: 5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, she has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.
On the other hand, respondent is placed exparte.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under;

Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8.
ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined herself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
She has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report,
Ex.P.6 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the Notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.8 is the Reply Notice,
Ex.P.9 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.10 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.11 is the Notarized copy of Driving License, Ex.P.12 is the Discharge summary and Ex.P.13 is the Medical Bills.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 22.12.2023 at about 08.30 a.m.,
petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EU-7084 which was droven by her husband slowly and cautiously with observing all traffic rules and regulations,
when approached Om Road took 'U' turn near Battarahalli Junction, at that time the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265 came in high speed, rash and negligent manner came against the one way in the opposite direction without observing the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Bowring Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.417/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279,
337 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.

In short, it is want Deepu. M vs Sunitha on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3694835/
3 of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the K. R. Puram Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 417/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, she got marked Ex.P1 to 9 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending motorcycle.

The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama and Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.9, Charge- Sheet against the driver of the offending Auto-rickshaw U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Reports discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
The evidence of the petitioner is not challenged by the respondent.

As stated above respondent already placed ex- parte.
15.

In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.

sentences.text: In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Bowring Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.
18. In the petition as well as in her evidence PW.1 deposed that, immediately after the accident she was shifted to Bowring Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient.

The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.12 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Medical College and Research Institute Hospital,
Bangalore from 22.12.2023 to 03.01.2024 i.e., for 12 day.

sentences.text:
She has produced the wound certificate Deepu. M vs Sunitha on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3694835/
4 marked at Ex.P.6 the doctor has opined that the injuries are simple in nature.
19. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

In support of her plea, he has produced 28 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.13 to the tune of Rs.17,566/-.
20.
In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that she has become permanently disabled.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- including the medical expenses.
21. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-9265 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
in view of above discussion, the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
22. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent being owner of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as it is meager.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.

Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
